password_hash.description: The bcrypt hash of the user's password, as fit hash-password or htpasswd -B makes it.

username.description: The user's name; it may not contain a colon.

ca_file.description: A PEM file of the certificates the directory's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of one's own.

challenges.description: The challenges answered, in the order tried: http-01, which the CA checks on port 80 at the name, answered by any listener of fit's in the clear, and tls-alpn-01, which it checks on port 443, answered by the TLS listener that lists the name. A failed attempt is tried again with the next. Both, http-01 first, when left out.

directory.description: The URL of the CA's ACME directory. Let's Encrypt's when left out; https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory is its staging CA, for tests.

email.description: The address the CA may write to about the account's certificates; none when left out.

max_concurrent.description: How many certificates are obtained at once; the rest wait their turn. 2 when left out or 0.

on_demand.description: How certificates are obtained during handshakes, for listeners whose tls sets on_demand: whom to ask whether a name may have one, and how fast and how many.

request_timeout.description: How long each request to the CA may take. 30s when left out.

storage.description: The directory accounts, keys and certificates are kept in, which instances of fit may share. $XDG_DATA_HOME/fit, or ~/.local/share/fit, when left out.

timeout.description: How long obtaining one certificate may take, challenges included, before it is given up and tried again later. 10m when left out.

buffer_bytes.description: How many bytes of lines may wait to be written; lines past it are dropped. 4 MiB when left out.

flush_interval.description: How long a line may wait in the buffer before it is written; 1s when left out.

output.description: "stdout", "stderr", or the path of a file lines are appended to; "stdout" when left out.

address.description: Where the Admin API listens: a host and port, or "unix/" and the path of a Unix socket, as in "unix//run/fit/admin.sock". The host must be a loopback address or localhost unless token_file is set. 127.0.0.1:2019 when left out.

history.description: How many of the configs applied, the running one included, are kept to be read back. 10 when left out or 0.

max_config_bytes.description: The largest config the Admin API takes; a larger one gets 413. 4 MiB when left out or 0.

max_conns.description: The most connections the Admin API keeps open at once; one past it is closed as soon as it is accepted. 16 when left out or 0.

token_file.description: A file holding a token that every request must carry, as "Authorization: Bearer <token>"; no token is asked for when left out.

disable.description: Turn HTTPS by default off: no listeners are made for a config that writes none, and an empty tls gets no certificates.

disable_redirects.description: Make no listener in the clear to redirect to HTTPS. ACME's HTTP-01 challenge is then answered by none, and certificates come through TLS-ALPN-01.

http_port.description: The port of the listener in the clear that redirects to HTTPS. 80 when left out or 0.

https_port.description: The port of the HTTPS listener, and the one redirects name when it is not 443. 443 when left out or 0.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the certificate, followed by any intermediates.

key_file.description: A PEM file with the certificate's private key.

ca_files.description: PEM files of the certificate authorities a client's certificate must chain to. They are watched as certificate files are: a change loads the config again.

mode.description: require: a client without a valid certificate is refused in the handshake; verify_if_given: a client may send none, and a route that needs one says so with the client_cert middleware, but one it sends must be valid. require when left out. A listener that requires certificates cannot answer ACME's TLS-ALPN-01 challenge, whose CA sends none.

endpoint.description: Where the Docker daemon's API is: unix:// and a socket's path, or tcp:// and a host and port, as of a socket proxy, in plain HTTP. unix:///var/run/docker.sock when left out.

expose_all.description: Take every running container with routes or services in its labels; only those labelled <label_prefix>.enable=true when left out or false. A container labelled <label_prefix>.enable=false is never taken.

label_prefix.description: What the labels read start with, as in fit.routes.web.host. fit when left out.

max_containers.description: The most containers taken; past it, the rest, by name, are left out and reported. 1000 when left out or 0.

network.description: The Docker network whose address of a container's is used, when the container is on several and has no <label_prefix>.network label; the first by name when left out.

refresh_interval.description: How often the containers are listed again whether or not an event came, in case one was missed. 30s when left out.

request_timeout.description: How long listing the containers may take, connecting included. 10s when left out.

use_published_ports.description: Send to the port a container's port is published on, on the host, rather than to the container's own address: for a fit outside Docker that cannot reach containers' addresses, as on Docker Desktop.

allow.description: The destinations the proxy connects to: host names, "*.example.com" for every name below example.com, IP addresses and CIDR ranges, which also hold the address a host name resolves to. Every destination deny does not hold when left out.

clients.description: The addresses and CIDR ranges of the clients that may use the proxy, as "10.0.0.0/8"; others are refused.

connect_timeout.description: How long resolving and connecting to a destination may take. 10s when left out.

deny.description: Destinations refused, written as in allow, whatever allow holds: a host name that resolves to an address deny holds is refused once it is connected, before anything is sent.

idle_timeout.description: How long a proxied connection may carry nothing either way before both sides are closed. 5m when left out.

ports.description: The destination ports allowed; any when left out.

expect_status.description: With http: the statuses that pass; any from 200 to 399 when left out.

fails.description: How many probes in a row must fail to take an address out of rotation; 2 when left out or 0.

host.description: With http: the Host field the probe sends; the address's host when left out.

interval.description: How long from the start of one probe of an address to the start of the next; 5s when left out.

jitter.description: Up to how much longer than interval each wait between probes may be, chosen at random each time, so that probes from many upstreams spread out; a tenth of interval when left out. Less than interval.

passes.description: How many probes in a row must pass to put an address that was out back in; 2 when left out or 0.

path.description: With http: the path, and query, the probe asks for; / when left out.

port.description: The port probes go to, in place of each address's own.

timeout.description: How long a probe may take, connecting included, before it fails; 2s when left out. No longer than interval.

type.description: http sends a GET request, over the upstream's protocol, and passes on an expected status; tcp passes once a connection opens. http when left out.

backends.description: Where requests to a Service go: endpoints, to its ready endpoints from its EndpointSlices, balanced by fit; or cluster_ip, to its cluster IP, balanced by the cluster. endpoints when left out.

context.description: The kubeconfig's context to use; its current-context when left out.

controller_name.description: The controllerName of the GatewayClasses whose Gateways fit serves. lesismal.github.io/fit when left out.

kubeconfig.description: A kubeconfig file to reach the cluster with: its server, CA, client certificate, token or token file. When left out, the pod's service account, inside the cluster, or else $KUBECONFIG or ~/.kube/config. Exec and auth-provider plugins are not supported.

listen_host.description: The IP address Gateway listeners are bound on, each on its port; every address when left out.

max_objects.description: The most objects of each kind kept: past it, the rest are left out and reported. 10000 when left out or 0.

namespaces.description: The namespaces whose Gateways and HTTPRoutes are served; every namespace when left out. Resources are watched across the cluster either way, so fit's account needs to list and watch them cluster-wide.

request_timeout.description: How long each request to the API server may take, but watches, which last five minutes each. 10s when left out.

max_body_bytes.description: The largest request body a listener takes, whether it arrives whole or streams through; a larger one gets 413, or, once it has begun to stream, its connection or stream is ended. 16 MiB when left out or 0.

max_conns.description: The most client connections the listeners keep open at once, across all of them; one past it is closed as soon as it is accepted. Takes effect at start, not on a reload. 100000 when left out or 0.

max_header_bytes.description: The largest request header a listener takes; a larger one gets 431. 1 MiB when left out or 0.

max_pending_bytes.description: How many bytes of responses may wait, across every connection, for clients to take them; past it, every connection stops reading until some go. 256 MiB when left out or 0.

write_stall_timeout.description: How long a response may wait for its client to take what it was sent, each time it waits, before the client loses it: its HTTP/1 connection closed, its HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 stream reset. A client that keeps reading, however slowly, is not cut off, and nor is a response that has nothing to send. 30s when left out.

address.description: The host and port to listen on, as in ":8080" or "127.0.0.1:8080".

name.description: A name unique among the listeners, by which routes refer to this one.

protocols.description: The protocols served: http/1.1, h2c (HTTP/2 in the clear) and, with tls, h2 (HTTP/2 over TLS, chosen through ALPN) and h3 (HTTP/3 over QUIC, on the same port in UDP, announced to HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 clients with Alt-Svc); tcp, raw TCP, whose connections the services that list the listener proxy to their upstreams; socks, a SOCKS5 and SOCKS4 forward proxy, as socks says; or udp alone, whose datagrams a service proxies. A listener that serves more than one of HTTP, tcp and socks tells them apart on its port by what a client sends first: a TLS ClientHello goes to the service whose server_names hold its name, or else, with tls, is served HTTPS, or else goes to the service without server_names; a SOCKS greeting to socks; an HTTP request, in the clear, to HTTP; and whatever else to the service without server_names, or it is closed. A client that waits for the server to speak first is closed after 10s: such a protocol needs a listener of its own. http/1.1 alone when left out, or http/1.1 and h2 with tls.

proxy_protocol.description: Take a PROXY protocol header, of version 1 or 2, at the start of each connection from a trusted address, and serve the connection as from the client it names. For listeners of tcp and of HTTP over TCP; with tls the header comes before TLS. HTTP/3 takes none.

socks.description: Who may use the listener's socks, and where it connects them: needed with socks. It serves CONNECT, without authentication, and refuses BIND and UDP ASSOCIATE.

tls.description: Serve TLS, with these certificates: the listener's HTTP is HTTPS.

expr.description: An expression the request must match, combining matchers with &&, ||, ! and parentheses, as in Host("a.example") && (PathPrefix("/api/") || Method("POST")). Its matchers are Host, Path, PathPrefix, PathRegexp, Method, Header(name, value...), Query(key, value...) and RemoteIP, whose arguments are strings quoted as in Go. It counts as one matcher in the order of routes, and its hosts and paths do not make a route more specific: give it a priority.

header.description: Headers the request must have, each with one of the values listed as the value of one of its fields, or with any value when none are listed. Names ignore case; values do not.

host.description: Host names, exact or with a leading "*." wildcard.

method.description: Methods, as in "GET"; compared as written, since methods are case-sensitive.

path.description: Paths, exact or ending in "*" to match a prefix.

path_regexp.description: Regular expressions in Go's syntax, matched against the path anywhere in it unless anchored with ^ and $.

query.description: Query parameters the request must have, each with one of the values listed, or with any value when none are listed; compared once unescaped.

remote_ip.description: IP addresses and CIDR prefixes, as in "10.0.0.0/8", the client's address must be in: the address of the connection, not of X-Forwarded-For.

ask.description: A URL fit asks, with the name in the query as domain=<name>, whether a name may have a certificate: an answer of 2xx allows it, and any other refuses it. Refusals are remembered for a minute.

idle_timeout.description: How long a name taken on demand is kept, and renewed, with no handshake asking for it; then it is dropped and no longer counts against max_names, and its certificate stays in the storage for the next handshake that asks for it, which the ask URL must allow again. 168h, a week, when left out.

interval.description: The interval rate counts over. 1m when left out.

max_names.description: How many names may have certificates obtained on demand, in all; past it, a handshake for another fails. 1000 when left out or 0.

rate.description: How many certificates may be obtained every interval; a handshake past it fails. 10 when left out or 0.

timeout.description: How long a handshake waits for its name's certificate, as long as fib's handshake timeout by default. 10s when left out.

docker.description: Routes, upstreams and services from the labels of running Docker containers.

kubernetes.description: Listeners, routes and upstreams from a Kubernetes cluster's Gateway API resources: the Gateways of the GatewayClasses whose controllerName is fit's, and their HTTPRoutes.

name.description: The name the provider goes by in the Admin API's /config/effective and in logs: lower-case letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-', unique among the providers. Its kind, as docker, when left out.

trusted.description: The addresses and CIDR ranges of the proxies that send the header, as "10.0.0.0/8": a connection from one of them must begin with a header, within 10s, or it is closed, and one from elsewhere is served as it is, with no header.

listeners.description: The names of the listeners the route serves; every listener when left out.

match.description: What a request must match; every request when left out.

middleware.description: Middleware a request passes through, in order, before the handler.

name.description: A name unique among the routes, for logs and metrics.

priority.description: Routes with a higher priority are picked first; among equal ones, the most specific host, then path, then the one with the most other matchers set (method, header, query, remote_ip, path_regexp, expr), then the one written first.

idle_timeout.description: How long a connection or a udp session may carry nothing either way before both sides are closed; 10m for a connection and 1m for a udp session when left out.

listeners.description: The names of the listeners whose connections the service takes: those that serve tcp, alone or beside other protocols, and udp listeners, each one service's. A udp listener's session is a client's address: the datagrams it sends go to one upstream address, from a socket of the session's own, and what comes back to that socket goes to the client.

max_conns.description: The most connections and udp sessions the service proxies at once; a connection past it is closed as soon as it is accepted, and the datagrams of a session past it are dropped. 10000 when left out or 0.

name.description: A name unique among the services.

proxy_protocol.description: Send each upstream connection a PROXY protocol header of this version (v1, text, or v2, binary) first, naming the client's address and the one it connected to. For tcp listeners.

server_names.description: The server names (SNI) of the TLS connections the service takes from its tcp listeners, which it proxies as they are, without terminating their TLS; "*.example.com" takes the names one label below example.com. A tcp listener may then be listed by several services: a connection goes to the one whose names hold the name its ClientHello asks for, or else to the listener's service without server_names, if it has one, as one that is not TLS or asks for no name does; otherwise it is closed. The ClientHello must come within 10s.

upstream.description: The name of the upstream connections go to: one of its addresses, picked by its load_balancing (ip_hash by the client's address; header, cookie and URI hashes, which a connection has none of, in turn), out of rotation for its max_fails and health checks as for HTTP, dialed within its connect_timeout. A connect that fails is tried on the next address picked, up to three addresses. Its protocol and HTTP settings are not used.

max_age.description: How long the client keeps the cookie, as its Max-Age; until the browser closes when left out.

name.description: The cookie's name; fit_sticky when left out.

path.description: The cookie's Path; / when left out.

secure.description: Mark the cookie Secure, so that it is sent only over HTTPS. It is always HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.

acme.description: Host names to obtain certificates for with ACME, as the top-level acme says, through its challenges: the CA must reach fit at each name on port 80, where any listener of fit's in the clear answers HTTP-01, or on port 443, where this listener answers TLS-ALPN-01. A client asking for one of these names is given its certificate once there is one; until then, and for other names, the certificates from files.

certificates.description: Certificates from files. A client is given the first whose names match the one it asks for, or the first of all when none does or it asks for none.

client_auth.description: Ask clients for certificates and verify them (mutual TLS).

on_demand.description: Obtain a certificate during the handshake for a name a client asks for that neither the files nor acme have, as the top-level acme.on_demand allows; needs it.

addresses.description: The addresses of the upstream's servers, each a host and a port, as in "10.0.0.1:8080" or "backend:80".

connect_timeout.description: How long opening a connection may take; 10s when left out. A request whose connect times out gets 504.

fail_timeout.description: The window max_fails are counted in, and how long an address that reached them stays out; 10s when left out.

hash_key.description: With header_hash, the header, and with cookie_hash, the cookie, whose value requests are hashed by.

health_check.description: Probe each address on a schedule, and take one that fails its probes out of rotation until it passes them again; no probes when left out. Probes and max_fails take an address out each on their own account.

idle_timeout.description: How long an idle connection is kept before it is closed; 60s when left out.

load_balancing.description: How requests are spread over the addresses: round_robin, in turn; weighted_round_robin, in turn by weight (smoothly, as nginx does); least_conn, to the address with the fewest requests under way for its weight; random, at random by weight; p2c, to the less busy for its weight of two addresses chosen at random; ip_hash, uri_hash, header_hash and cookie_hash, by a consistent hash of the client's IP address, the request's path and query, the header hash_key names or the cookie it names, so that the same key goes to the same address while it is up, and adding or removing an address moves only the keys that went to it or will. A request without the header or cookie goes in turn. round_robin when left out, or weighted_round_robin when weights are given.

max_conns.description: The most connections open, or being opened, to one address; a request past it waits for one to be free. 256 when left out or 0.

max_fails.description: How many failed requests to an address within fail_timeout take it out of rotation for fail_timeout, as nginx's max_fails does: a connect that failed, an upstream that broke off or timed out. 1 when left out; 0 keeps every address in rotation.

max_idle_conns.description: How many idle connections to one address are kept for later requests; 32 when left out, and 0 keeps none.

max_pending.description: How many requests may wait for a connection to one address once its max_conns are busy; one past it is answered 503 at once. 1024 when left out or 0.

name.description: A name unique among the upstreams, by which handlers refer to this one.

protocol.description: How requests reach the upstream: http/1.1 in the clear, h2c (HTTP/2 in the clear, which the servers must expect), or h2 (TLS, with HTTP/2 when the server chooses it through ALPN and HTTP/1.1 otherwise). http/1.1 when left out.

response_header_timeout.description: How long the upstream may take, once the request is sent, to begin its response; 60s when left out. A request past it gets 504.

response_idle_timeout.description: How long the upstream may go silent in the middle of a response body; 60s when left out.

response_timeout.description: How long a whole response may take, from sending the request to the end of its body; 1h when left out. A request past it before its response began gets 504, and one past it later is cut short.

sticky_cookie.description: Keep each client on one address with a cookie: a request whose cookie names an address that is up goes there, and any other gets the cookie for the address it went to. No cookie when left out.

tls_ca_file.description: With h2: a PEM file of the certificates the servers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots. It is watched, as a listener's certificate files are: a change loads the config again.

tls_cert_file.description: With h2: a PEM file of the client certificate, and the chain after it, that fit presents to servers that ask for one (mutual TLS); needs tls_key_file. It is watched, as tls_ca_file is: a change loads the config again.

tls_key_file.description: With h2: the PEM file of tls_cert_file's private key.

tls_server_name.description: With h2: the name the servers' certificates are checked against, and sent in SNI; each address's host when left out.

weights.description: Each address's weight, in the order of addresses: its share of requests under weighted_round_robin, and how many requests it takes to be as busy as an address of weight 1 under least_conn. 1 each when left out.

add.description: Values to add to fields, after any already there.

delete.description: Fields to delete: names, or a prefix ending in "*", as in "X-Debug-*".

set.description: Fields to set, each replacing any of the same name.

module.description: The module's name within its namespace.

allow.description: The destinations the proxy connects to: host names, "*.example.com" for every name below example.com, IP addresses and CIDR ranges, which also hold the address a host name resolves to. Every destination deny does not hold when left out; others are answered 403, or 502 for a host name whose address decides.

clients.description: The addresses and CIDR ranges of the clients that may use the proxy, as "10.0.0.0/8"; others are answered 403.

connect_timeout.description: How long resolving and connecting to a destination may take; past it the request is answered 504. 10s when left out.

deny.description: Destinations refused, written as in allow, whatever allow holds.

idle_timeout.description: How long a tunnel may carry nothing either way before it and its connection to the destination are closed. 5m when left out.

ports.description: The destination ports allowed; any when left out.

failover.description: An upstream that takes the requests when none of the chosen upstream's backends is in rotation, for failing or for its health checks, and one of its own is.

host_header.description: The Host header sent upstream; the client's when left out.

mirror.description: Send a copy of a share of the requests whose bodies arrive whole (64KB at most) to another upstream, and drop its answers. At most 256 copies are under way at once; past that, requests are not copied. The requests themselves do not wait for their copies.

retry.description: Send a request that failed again, to the backend the upstream picks next: one whose connection could not be made, whatever its method, and, for GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT and DELETE, one that failed before its response began or was answered with a status of statuses. A request whose body streams (past 64KB, or still arriving) is never sent again. No retries when left out.

timeout.description: The most a request may take, from when the proxy takes it to the end of its response, retries included: one past it before its response began is answered 504, and one whose response is under way is cut short. None when left out.

trusted_proxies.description: The addresses ("10.0.0.1") and networks ("10.0.0.0/8") of proxies in front of this one, whose X-Forwarded-* and Forwarded fields are believed. None when left out.

tunnel_idle_timeout.description: How long a tunnel, as a WebSocket the proxy has joined to its upstream is, may carry nothing either way before it is closed; 10m when left out.

upstream.description: The name of the upstream requests go to; or upstreams.

upstreams.description: Upstreams requests are spread over at random by weight, as a canary release does, in place of upstream.

headers.description: Response headers. Content-Type defaults to text/plain; charset=utf-8 when there is a body.

status.description: The status code; 200 when left out.

browse.description: List a directory that has no index file, rather than answering 404. Files whose names start with a dot are left out.

browse_max_entries.description: The most entries a listing reads and shows; a directory with more is listed in part, and says so. 10000 when left out or 0.

check_interval.description: How long what the handler learned of a request path, the file it names and its validators, is trusted before the disk is looked at again; a change on disk shows within it. 1s when left out.

index.description: The files that stand for a directory, tried in order; ["index.html"] when left out, and none for [].

max_cache_bytes.description: How many bytes of files are kept in memory at most; 64 MiB when left out.

max_file_bytes.description: The largest file kept in memory, in bytes; 1 MiB when left out.

precompressed.description: Encodings whose compressed twins, name.br, name.zst and name.gz, are served in place of a file to a client that accepts them: the one it prefers by Accept-Encoding, and among equals the first listed. None when left out.

root.description: The directory files are served from.

strip_prefix.description: A prefix removed from the request path before it is looked up under the root; a request whose path lacks it gets 404.

try_files.description: Paths tried in turn for a request, as nginx's try_files: {path} stands for the request's path, and one ending in / for a directory, served by its index file. The first that exists is served, and when none does the answer is 404; ["{path}", "{path}/", "/index.html"] serves a single-page app. A directory asked for without its slash is not redirected then.

module.description: The module's name within its namespace.

forward_authorization.description: Leave the Authorization field, with the password, on the request the handler sees; it is removed when left out.

realm.description: The realm the browser shows when it asks for a user and password; fit when left out.

user_header.description: A request field to set to the user's name for the handler, and the upstream a proxy sends the request to; any the client sent is replaced.

users.description: The users allowed in, with their passwords' bcrypt hashes.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes a request's body may have.

error_ratio.description: The share of failures in the window that opens it; 0.5 when left out.

half_open_requests.description: How many requests it lets through, half-open, that must all fare well for it to close; 5 when left out. Others are answered 503 meanwhile.

min_requests.description: How many requests the window must have counted before it can open; 20 when left out.

open_duration.description: How long it stays open before letting requests through to try; 30s when left out.

slow_ratio.description: With slow_threshold, the share of slow responses in the window that opens it; 0.5 when left out.

slow_threshold.description: A response that takes longer than this to begin counts as slow; none is when left out.

statuses.description: The statuses that count as failures; 500 to 599 when left out.

window.description: How far back requests are counted, in ten steps; 10s when left out.

optional.description: Let a request without a certificate through as well, unauthenticated; refused with 403 Forbidden when left out.

subject_header.description: A request field to set to the certificate's subject, as in "CN=alice,O=Example", for the handler and the upstream a proxy sends the request to; any the client sent is removed, with or without a certificate.

encodings.description: The encodings offered, the one the client prefers most chosen, and among those it prefers as much, the first here; zstd, br and gzip when left out.

level.description: How hard the compressors work: fastest, default (gzip 5, zstd's default, brotli 4) or better (gzip 7, zstd's better, brotli 6); default when left out.

max_in_flight.description: How many responses are compressed at once; past it, responses go uncompressed, so that the compressors' memory, a few hundred kilobytes each, is bounded. 1024 when left out.

min_length.description: The shortest declared body compressed; 1024 when left out. A body that declares no length, as one that streams, is compressed.

max.description: The most requests under way at once.

status.description: The status of a request refused; 429 when left out, or 503 as nginx's limit_conn answers.

copy_headers.description: Fields copied from a 2xx answer onto the request, for the handler and the upstream a proxy sends it to. Any of these the client sent are removed, so that it cannot pass them off as the auth service's.

request_headers.description: The request's fields sent to the auth service; all but the hop-by-hop ones and those of the body when left out.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the auth service's answer, after which the request is answered 504 Gateway Timeout; 10s when left out. A service that cannot be reached is answered 502 Bad Gateway.

upstream.description: The name of the upstream the auth service is.

uri.description: The path, and query, of the request sent to the auth service; / when left out.

request.description: Changes to the request's fields, made before the handler, and the upstream a proxy sends the request to, sees them.

response.description: Changes to the response's fields, made just before it is sent, whichever handler wrote it.

algorithms.description: The algorithms tokens may be signed with; any that fits the keys when left out. none never is.

audience.description: Audiences of which a token's aud must name one; any when left out.

claims_headers.description: Request fields to set to claims, as {"X-User": "sub"}: a string as it is, anything else as JSON. Any of these fields the client sent are removed, with or without the claim.

hmac_secret_file.description: A file whose contents are the secret of tokens signed with HS256, HS384 or HS512; at least 32 bytes.

issuer.description: The iss a token must have; any when left out.

jwks_refresh.description: How often the JWK set is fetched again; 1h when left out. A token naming a kid the set does not have has it fetched sooner, at most every 10s.

jwks_url.description: The URL of a JWK set (RFC 7517) whose signing keys tokens are verified with.

leeway.description: How far exp and nbf may be off, for clocks that differ; none when left out.

public_key_files.description: PEM files of public keys or certificates (RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519) tokens are verified with.

token_from.description: Where the token is: header, after Bearer in the Authorization field; header:Name, the whole of that field; cookie:name; or query:name. header when left out.

burst.description: How many requests a key may make at once, after it has been idle: the bucket's size. The rate, rounded up, when left out.

key.description: What requests are counted by: ip, the client's address; route, every request of the route together; or header:Name, a header's value, with a request without it counted by ip. ip when left out.

max_keys.description: The most keys kept at once, which bounds the memory the buckets take: under 100 bytes each, and up to 128 more for a header; 100000 when left out or 0.

rate.description: How many requests a second each key may make, on average; at least 0.001.

status.description: The status of a request refused; 429 when left out.

trusted_proxies.description: The addresses ("10.0.0.1") and networks ("10.0.0.0/8") of proxies in front of fit: for a request that comes from one, the client's address is the last in X-Forwarded-For that is not one of them. None when left out, and the client is the connection's peer.

regexp.description: A regular expression in Go's syntax that the path must match for the request to be redirected; the rest go on to the handler. Every request is redirected when left out.

status.description: The status: 301 and 308 are permanent, 302, 303 and 307 temporary; 307 and 308 keep the method and body. 302 when left out.

to.description: Where to: a URL or a path, in which {scheme}, {host} (with its port, as the client sent it), {path}, {query} (without the '?') and {uri} (the path and query) stand for the request's, and, with regexp, $1 or ${name} for its groups, as in "https://{host}{uri}" or "/new/$1".

add_prefix.description: A prefix put before the path, as in "/v2".

regexp.description: A regular expression in Go's syntax; each match in the path is replaced with replacement.

replacement.description: What replaces each match of regexp, in which $1 or ${name} stand for the regexp's groups.

strip_prefix.description: Prefixes to take off the path: the first that the path starts with, at a segment boundary, is removed, and what is left starts with '/'. "/api" makes "/api/users" "/users" and "/api" "/", and leaves "/apix" alone.

percent.description: The share of requests copied, chosen at random; all of them when left out.

upstream.description: The name of the upstream the copies go to.

attempts.description: How many times a request may be sent again after the first; 2 when left out.

budget_min_per_second.description: Retries allowed each second beyond budget_ratio, so that a proxy taking few requests may still retry; 10 when left out.

budget_ratio.description: Retries may add at most this share of the requests the proxy takes, so that retries cannot multiply the load on an upstream already failing; 0.2 when left out.

statuses.description: Statuses of the upstream's, 5xx ones, that have a request of an idempotent method sent again, as 502, 503 and 504; none when left out, so that only requests that got no response are.

weight.description: Its share of the requests, against the others' weights.

access_log.description: Where a line is written for each request, as JSON; no access log when left out.

acme.description: How certificates for the names listeners list in tls.acme are obtained and renewed; the defaults when left out. Its settings are read when fit starts: a change to them takes effect when fit restarts. The names follow every reload.

admin.description: The Admin API, through which the running config is read and replaced, and which serves metrics in Prometheus's text format at /metrics; off when left out. Its settings are read when fit starts: a change to them takes effect when fit restarts.

auto_https.description: HTTPS by default: a config that writes no listeners is served over HTTPS on port 443, with certificates obtained with acme for the host names its routes match, and over HTTP on port 80 only to be redirected; a listener whose tls is empty gets certificates for the host names of the routes it serves. On when left out.

limits.description: Limits that apply to every listener.

listeners.description: The addresses fit listens on, and the protocols each one serves. When left out, HTTPS by default makes them from the routes' host names; see auto_https.

metrics.description: Count and time requests by listener and route, for the Admin API's /metrics, which serves the rest of fit's metrics without it; off when left out, since it costs every request a little. Needs admin.

providers.description: Sources of routes, upstreams, services and listeners other than this file and the Admin API, merged into the config: what this config writes wins over every provider, and a provider over those listed after it; a provider's element named as one before it is left out. The Admin API's /config/effective shows the result and where each part came from. Read when fit starts: a change takes effect when fit restarts.

routes.description: How requests are matched, and what handles them.

services.description: Layer 4 services: the upstreams the connections of tcp listeners are proxied to, byte for byte, and the datagrams of udp listeners, one for one.

upstreams.description: The servers requests can be proxied to, by name.
